headline: High: CrewAI’s writable, broad-egress orchestration can feed Pipecat’s shared-bus pipelines, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and run browsers/subprocesses, while Pipecat uses stdin/stdout and shared-bus session state. That creates a plausible content bridge where CrewAI-produced files or messages can be consumed by Pipecat as trusted input. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace that Pipecat reads
IF Pipecat ingests stdin/stdout or bus messages without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic file ingestion in Pipecat
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Review any shared bus consumers before enabling them
requires-engineering: add an allowlist parser for CrewAI outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data and API keys, and has broad network egress; Pipecat handles text, conversation state, audio/video, and can call many third-party model/STT/TTS services. If they share a workspace or message bus, sensitive content can flow from CrewAI into Pipecat’s external API calls. The exact bridge is undocumented, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or bus
IF Pipecat forwards conversation state or text to external STT/LLM/TTS providers
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of shared folders
Use separate API keys per agent
Disable external providers in Pipecat for sensitive runs
Redact secrets before handing data to CrewAI
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Pipecat supports multiple instances with shared-bus state. Overlapping mutable access can cause races or clobbered artifacts if both operate on the same resources. Because Pipecat’s write scope is not explicit, I cannot justify high severity and must escalate uncertainty only to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared bus
IF orchestration does not provide locking or per-agent namespaces
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Namespace shared-bus topics by agent
Avoid concurrent runs on the same artifacts
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration layer that can emit tool outputs and intermediate facts, while Pipecat is a real-time voice/chat pipeline with many downstream services. If Pipecat treats CrewAI output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected instruction can cascade into spoken responses or external actions. The default-path interaction is dangerous enough to rate high.
conditions: IF Pipecat consumes CrewAI output without verification
IF downstream services act on that output in real time
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step
Require structured schemas for CrewAI outputs
Log and review high-impact actions before execution
Disable auto-actioning in Pipecat pipelines
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before acting

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Pipecat processes text, audio, video, and analytics/metrics and can send them to third-party providers. If regulated content such as EU PII or sensitive recordings enters Pipecat’s external services, retention and residency obligations may diverge from CrewAI’s local orchestration assumptions. The profiles do not document matching controls, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through Pipecat providers
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of external Pipecat services
Review provider DPAs before enabling them
Minimize logs and analytics fields
Separate compliant and non-compliant workloads
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
